data.long_meaning: Rushabhaj is a Hindu name for Lord Krishna, who is considered the Lord of the Cattle. The name Rushabhaj carries the meaning “Lord of the Cattle” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Rushabhaj usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the cattle and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference:
Rushabhaj Amoghvarsha was a Jain monk and the 19th Tirthankara of Jainism.
According to Jain legend, Rushabhaj was born in the Sravasti region of ancient India, around 400 BC.
He renounced worldly life at a young age and lived an ascetic life, preaching the Jain doctrine of non-violence and self-control.
He is revered by Jains as a spiritual teacher and savior.

Rushabh Dev or Rushabhaj is another name for the Hindu god Rama, the hero of the Indian epic Ramayana.
According to Hindu mythology, Rushabhaj was the king of Ayodhya and the eldest son of King Dasharatha.
He ruled justly and with great wisdom, but was exiled from his kingdom due to a prophecy that predicted his father's death during his reign.
He lived in the forest, along with his wife Sita and his brother Lakshmana, and later returned to claim his throne.
